title: Problem Statement, References, and Imports
content: The module docstring sets up Erdős Problem #1097: estimating $|D(A)|$ for $n$-element sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$. The known bounds $n^{1.778} \leq |D(A)| \leq n^{11/6}$ and the conjectured $O(n^{3/2})$ are stated, along with the connection to Bourgain's sums-differences problem and the Kakeya conjecture. Three Mathlib imports provide tactics, finite sets, and real powers. The `open Finset` declaration enables direct use of `Finset.filter`, `Finset.image`, etc.
mathContext: The problem asks: for $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $|A| = n$, is $|D(A)| = O(n^{3/2})$? Current bounds: $n^{1.778} \leq \max_{|A|=n} |D(A)| \leq C \cdot n^{11/6}$.

title: IsThreeAP
content: A three-term arithmetic progression with base $a$ and common difference $d$ in set $A$: the elements $a$, $a+d$, $a+2d$ all belong to $A$. This is the fundamental predicate underlying the entire formalization.
mathContext: A three-term AP is a triple $(a, a+d, a+2d)$ with $a, a+d, a+2d \in A$. Equivalently, three elements $x < y < z$ form an AP iff $y - x = z - y$, i.e., $2y = x + z$.

title: Common Differences D(A)
content:
The set $D(A)$ of all integers $d$ such that some three-term AP in $A$ has common difference $d$. This is the central object studied in Problem #1097: understanding how $|D(A)|$ grows with $|A|$.

**Structural properties of $D(A)$:** Since $a, a+d, a+2d \in A$ implies $a+2d, (a+2d)-d, (a+2d)-2d \in A$, the set $D(A)$ is symmetric: $d \in D(A) \iff -d \in D(A)$. For dense sets $A \subseteq [n]$ with $|A| = \delta n$, counting arguments give $|D(A)| \geq \Omega(n)$ (at least one AP exists for most differences $d$). The deep question is whether $|D(A)|$ can be polynomially larger than $|A|$ — i.e., whether dense sets necessarily exhibit many *distinct* AP common differences.
mathContext: $D(A) = \{d \in \mathbb{Z} : \exists\, a \text{ s.t. } a, a+d, a+2d \in A\}$. Note $0 \in D(A)$ whenever $A \neq \emptyset$, and $D(A)$ is symmetric: $d \in D(A) \Leftrightarrow -d \in D(A)$.

title: Finite Versions: commonDiffFinset and numCommonDiff
content: Computable finite-set versions of $D(A)$. The function `commonDiffFinset` filters the difference set $A - A$ for those $d$ admitting a witness, and `numCommonDiff` returns $|D(A)|$. These enable concrete computations and cardinality bounds.
mathContext: $D(A) \subseteq A - A$, so $|D(A)| \le |A - A| \le |A|^2$. The filter checks $\exists\, a \in A : a + d \in A \wedge a + 2d \in A$.

title: Subset Bound, Cardinality, and Nonemptiness
content: Foundational facts proved without axioms: (1) `commonDiffFinset_subset`: $D(A) \subseteq A - A$ via `filter_subset`. (2) `numCommonDiff_le_card_sq`: $|D(A)| \leq |A|^2$ since $|A - A| \leq |A|^2$. (3) `zero_mem_commonDiffFinset`: $0 \in D(A)$ for nonempty $A$ (every element forms a trivial AP $a, a, a$), hence `numCommonDiff_pos`: $|D(A)| \geq 1$. (4) `commonDiffFinset_empty`: $D(\emptyset) = \emptyset$.
mathContext: $D(A) \subseteq A - A \implies |D(A)| \leq |A - A| \leq |A|^2$. Nonemptiness: $a \in A \implies a, a+0, a+2 \cdot 0 \in A$, so $0 \in D(A)$. Empty set: $D(\emptyset) = \emptyset$.

title: Monotonicity, Small-Set Computations, and Symmetry
content: The `commonDiffFinset_mono` and `numCommonDiff_mono` theorems establish monotonicity: $A \subseteq B \implies D(A) \subseteq D(B)$, proved by showing that any AP witness in $A$ is also a witness in $B$. Also includes `neg_mem_commonDiffFinset` (Finset-level symmetry: $d \in D(A) \implies -d \in D(A)$), tighter bound $|D(A)| \leq |A - A|$, and exact computations for small sets: singletons have $D(\{a\}) = \{0\}$, pairs $D(\{a,b\}) = \{0\}$ (no non-trivial 3-AP in a 2-element set), and count monotonicity.
mathContext: Monotonicity: $A \subseteq B \implies D(A) \subseteq D(B) \implies |D(A)| \leq |D(B)|$. Symmetry: $d \in D(A) \implies -d \in D(A)$. Small sets: $D(\{a\}) = \{0\}$, $D(\{a,b\}) = \{0\}$.

title: Negation Symmetry and Finset-Set Lifting
content: `commonDifferences_neg_iff`: $d \in D(A) \iff -d \in D(A)$ — if $a, a+d, a+2d \in A$ then reversing gives $a+2d, (a+2d)-d, (a+2d)-2d \in A$ with common difference $-d$. `commonDiffFinset_mem_commonDifferences`: lifts Finset membership to Set-level membership, connecting the computable and propositional definitions.
mathContext: $D(A) = -D(A)$: the AP $(a, a+d, a+2d)$ reversed is $(a+2d, a+d, a)$ with difference $-d$. Combined with $0 \in D(A)$, this means $|D(A)|$ is always odd for finite $A$ (symmetric around 0 plus the element 0 itself).

title: Translation Invariance: D(A + c) = D(A)
content: `commonDiffFinset_translate`: translating every element of $A$ by a constant $c$ does not change the common differences. Proof: an AP $(a', a'+d, a'+2d)$ in $A + c$ corresponds to $(a'-c, a'-c+d, a'-c+2d)$ in $A$ with the same difference $d$. Both directions proved via `ext d` and `Finset.mem_image` destructuring. This is the additive analogue of the principle that distance sets are translation-invariant.
mathContext: $D(A + c) = D(A)$ for all $c \in \mathbb{Z}$. If $(a+c, a+c+d, a+c+2d) \in (A+c)^3$ then $(a, a+d, a+2d) \in A^3$ with the same $d$.

title: Dilation Covariance and Concrete AP Computations
content: `commonDiff_dilation`: if $d \in D(A)$ then $cd \in D(cA)$ — scaling the set scales the common differences. Proved by showing $(ca, ca+cd, ca+2cd) \in (cA)^3$ from $(a, a+d, a+2d) \in A^3$. Also computes $D(\{a, a+1, a+2\}) = \{-1, 0, 1\}$: the AP $(a, a+1, a+2)$ gives $d=1$, reversal gives $d=-1$, trivial gives $d=0$. Proves the 3-element consecutive set has exactly 3 common differences.
mathContext: Dilation: $d \in D(A) \implies cd \in D(cA)$. Example: $D(\{a, a+1, a+2\}) = \{-1, 0, 1\}$, so $|D| = 3$ for any 3-consecutive set.

title: Erdős's O(n^{3/2}) Conjecture
content:
The central open question: does $|D(A)| = O(n^{3/2})$? The Erdős-Spencer probabilistic construction achieves $\Omega(n^{3/2})$, so the conjecture asserts this is essentially tight. The answer determines the exact growth rate of common differences.

This connects to the broader landscape of additive combinatorics: Szemerédi's theorem (see `szemeredi-theorem`) guarantees that dense sets contain arbitrarily long APs, while this problem asks how many *distinct* common differences arise in 3-term APs. The Roth-type bounds (see `roth-theorem-k3`) on sets without 3-APs provide complementary constraints.
mathContext: The conjecture asks: $\exists\, C > 0$ such that for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $|A| = n$, $|D(A)| \le C \cdot n^{3/2}$. Combined with the Erdős-Spencer lower bound, this would give $|D(A)| = \Theta(n^{3/2})$.

title: Katz-Tao Upper Bound
content: The best known upper bound: $|D(A)| \le C \cdot n^{11/6}$ for some absolute constant $C$. Published by Nets Katz and Terence Tao in 1999, this improved earlier bounds using incidence geometry techniques related to the Kakeya problem.
mathContext: The exponent $11/6 \approx 1.833$ improved the trivial $|D(A)| \le |A-A| = O(n^2)$ bound. The proof uses a combinatorial geometry argument connecting the problem to line incidences in $\mathbb{R}^2$, mirroring techniques from the Kakeya conjecture.

title: Erdős-Spencer Lower Bound
content: A probabilistic construction showing $\Omega(n^{3/2})$ common differences exist. The argument uses the Lovász Local Lemma or second-moment methods to show random subsets of $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ achieve this bound with positive probability.
mathContext: There exists $C > 0$ such that for all $n$, some $A$ with $|A| = n$ satisfies $|D(A)| \ge C \cdot n^{3/2}$. This is the conjectured correct order; the gap with the Katz-Tao upper bound is between exponents $3/2 = 1.5$ and $11/6 \approx 1.833$.

title: Erdős-Ruzsa Explicit Construction
content: An explicit (derandomized) construction achieving $n^{1+c}$ common differences for some constant $c > 0$. Unlike the Erdős-Spencer probabilistic argument, this gives a concrete family of sets, though with a weaker exponent.
mathContext: There exist $c > 0$ and $C > 0$ such that for all $n$, an explicit $A$ with $|A| = n$ satisfies $|D(A)| \ge C \cdot n^{1+c}$. The exponent $1+c$ is weaker than the probabilistic $3/2$ but the construction is constructive.

title: Lemm's Lower Bound
content:
Matan Lemm (2015) proved the existence of sets achieving exponent $> 1.778$, surpassing the Erdős-Spencer $3/2 = 1.5$ barrier. This is the best known unconditional lower bound on the exponent.

**Significance of the exponent improvement:** The jump from $3/2$ to $1.778$ is substantial: it shows the true growth rate of $|D(A)|$ is strictly superlinear-times-polylogarithmic, ruling out a class of counting arguments that would give exactly $\Theta(n^{3/2})$. Lemm's construction uses probabilistic methods with careful moment estimates to build sets where many common differences are forced. The gap between $1.778$ (best lower bound on the exponent) and $11/6 \approx 1.833$ (Katz-Tao upper bound) remains the central open interval for this problem.
mathContext: There exists $c > 1.778$ such that for all $n$, some $A$ with $|A| = n$ satisfies $|D(A)| \ge n^c$. The improvement from $1.5$ to $1.778$ suggests the true exponent may be strictly between $3/2$ and $11/6$.

title: AlphaEvolve Improvement
content: Google DeepMind's AlphaEvolve (2025) achieved a marginal improvement over Lemm's bound using automated search methods, pushing the lower bound exponent slightly past $1.77898$. This represents one of the first AI contributions to this problem.
mathContext: The improvement is from $c > 1.778$ to $c > 1.77898$, a very small gain. The significance lies in the method: evolutionary search over construction parameters, suggesting AI-assisted extremal combinatorics as a new research direction.

title: Restricted Sum and Difference
content: Given a bipartite graph $G \subseteq A \times B$, the restricted sum $A +_G B = \{a + b : (a,b) \in G\}$ and restricted difference $A -_G B = \{a - b : (a,b) \in G\}$. These are central to Bourgain's formulation linking sumset problems to Kakeya-type questions.
mathContext: For $G \subseteq A \times B$: $A +_G B = \{a + b : (a,b) \in G\}$ and $A -_G B = \{a - b : (a,b) \in G\}$. When $G = A \times B$, these reduce to the usual sumset $A + B$ and difference set $A - B$.

title: Bourgain Exponent
content: The Bourgain sums-differences exponent $c$: the assertion that $|A -_G B| \le C \cdot \max(|A|, |B|, |A +_G B|)^c$ for all finite sets $A, B$ and graphs $G \subseteq A \times B$. This reformulates the 3-AP problem in the language of harmonic analysis.
mathContext: $\text{BourgainExponent}(c) :\Leftrightarrow \exists\, C > 0,\; \forall A, B, G \subseteq A \times B,\; |A -_G B| \le C \cdot \max(|A|, |B|, |A +_G B|)^c$. The critical exponent $c^*$ where this transitions from true to false equals the 3-AP exponent.

title: Chan's Equivalence Theorem
content: Chan proved that the optimal exponent for common differences in 3-APs equals the critical Bourgain sums-differences exponent. This deep equivalence bridges additive combinatorics with harmonic analysis and the Kakeya conjecture, meaning progress on either problem implies progress on the other.
mathContext: For $c \ge 1$: $(\forall n,\; \exists A,\; |A| = n,\; |D(A)| \ge n^c) \;\Leftrightarrow\; \neg\text{BourgainExponent}(c)$. In other words, $c^*_{\text{3-AP}} = c^*_{\text{Bourgain}}$. This links a discrete combinatorial problem to continuous Kakeya-type geometry.

title: Current Bounds Summary
content: The proven theorem combining Lemm's lower bound and Katz-Tao's upper bound: the critical exponent satisfies $1.778 < c^* \le 11/6$. This is derived directly from the axiomatized results, showing the formalization captures the current state of knowledge.
mathContext: The theorem states $1.778 < c^* \le 11/6 \approx 1.833$, where $c^*$ is the critical exponent for $|D(A)|$ growth. The gap of approximately $0.055$ between lower and upper bounds remains one of the key open problems in additive combinatorics.
